name: Streaming aggregation for observability metrics
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: The streaming-aggregation-for-observability segment in 2025-2026 is a dense, well-capitalised, OTel-first market. Six archetypes matter: (A) Prometheus-compatible TSDBs with streaming/recording-rule pre-aggregation: Grafana Mimir 3.0 (launched at KubeCon NA Nov 5 2025, AGPLv3, new Mimir Query Engine streams query results with up to 92% lower peak memory, Kafka inserted as async buffer between ingest and query, billion-active-series scale at Grafana Cloud), VictoriaMetrics (Apache-2.0 OSS + Enterprise license; first-class stream aggregation as the documented alternative to recording rules - documented 4-second-to-fraction-of-a-second query speedups; real production examples aggregating 114,765 series down to 785), Cortex (Mimir's CNCF predecessor, Apache-2.0), Thanos (Apache-2.0), M3DB (Apache-2.0 - Chronosphere's open-source roots, 500 M metrics/s aggregation, 20 M metrics/s persistence). (B) Specialised cardinality-control platforms: Chronosphere (acquired by Palo Alto Networks for $3.35 B announced Nov 19 2025, completed Jan 29 2026, $160 M+ ARR Sept 2025, triple-digit YoY growth, recognised Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader 2025; Control Plane delivers ~84% data reduction on average; M3-derived backend), Last9 Levitate (Sequoia India / Peak XV-backed, Gartner Cool Vendor 'AI for SRE Observability' 2025, 20 M+ cardinality per metric, streaming aggregation + Cardinality Explorer + Cardinality Calculator + workflows, public customers include Replit / Disney+ Hotstar / Clevertap / Circle / Probo / Quickwork), Honeycomb (Honeycomb Metrics GA Mar 11 2026, events-based unlimited-cardinality + time-series hybrid, $50 M Series D Apr 2023, AI-native suite Sept 2025, intro pricing $2 / 1k time series / mo), Grafana Cloud Adaptive Telemetry (Adaptive Metrics + Adaptive Logs + Adaptive Traces GA + Adaptive Profiles private preview, announced at ObservabilityCON 2025, ~35% metrics-cost reduction average across 1,500+ orgs, 20-50% time-series reduction with zero app changes). (C) Hyperscaler / proprietary metrics products: Datadog Metrics Without Limits (two-tier ingest-vs-index pricing, $0.10 / 100 ingested metric + $5 / 100 indexed metrics, 100 custom metrics/host included in Pro), Splunk Observability Cloud, Dynatrace Davis, New Relic, AWS Managed Service for Prometheus, Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus, Azure Monitor. (D) Telemetry-pipeline cardinality cutters (the 'shaping layer'): Cribl (general-purpose log/metrics router, market leader), Sawmills ($10 M seed 2025, AI-powered metric-cost recommendations), Edge Delta (telemetry pipelines free at any scale Apr 2026), Bindplane (Google-backed OTel-compatible), ControlTheory, Mezmo, Calyptia. (E) OSS columnar / ClickHouse-backed observability stacks: SigNoz (Apache-2.0, OTel-native, ClickHouse backend), OpenObserve (Apache-2.0, $0.30/GB ingest June 2025 pricing, single-binary, 140x-lower-storage-cost claim), HyperDX / ClickStack (HyperDX UI on ClickHouse), Uptrace, Parseable, Tinybird (real-time analytics platform, observability is a vertical use case, new pricing Jan 2025 / Pro-to-Developer migration Apr 2025), Apache SkyWalking, Netdata. (F) OTel-collector-native aggregation: spanmetrics connector (replaces spanmetrics processor, generates R.E.D. metrics from traces, 2025 enhancements support W3C tracestate extrapolation for sampled traces), statsdreceiver (default 60s aggregation interval), the OTel metrics data model's first-class temporal + spatial re-aggregation. Adjacent: Netflix Atlas, Pinot, Druid for OLAP-style metrics, ClickHouse-direct deployments via OTel Collector exporter. None of these are pure feature-servers in beava's sense; they all bundle ingest + storage + query + dashboards + alerting, with the streaming-aggregation feature as a sub-component that pre-aggregates labels away before they hit the TSDB index.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: For the streaming-aggregation-for-observability segment specifically, the named 2025-2026 incumbents are: Grafana Mimir 3.0 (Nov 2025) + Grafana Adaptive Telemetry (ObservabilityCON 2025) = the open-source-PromQL-canonical answer; VictoriaMetrics stream aggregation = the highest-perf Apache-2.0-OSS answer (the configuration is a single vmagent flag, runs before-the-DB, and is widely cited on the Mimir/Prometheus migration path); Chronosphere Control Plane (now Palo Alto Networks owned, $3.35 B Jan 2026) = the enterprise SaaS leader for cardinality-shaping, anchored on M3 / Thanos hybrid streaming + batch ingest pipeline; Last9 Levitate = the India-rooted streaming-aggregation-first challenger (Sequoia-India backed; explicit positioning 'unlike recording rules, aggregates in real-time as it arrives, massively reducing query overhead'); Honeycomb Metrics (GA Mar 2026) = the events-based-high-cardinality challenger that explicitly does NOT pre-aggregate (it stores raw events, columnar, and aggregates at query time) - structurally orthogonal to Beava's pre-aggregation thesis; Datadog Metrics Without Limits = the proprietary-vendor incumbent answer (decouples ingest from index, indexes only the tag subset you allowlist - functionally a server-side aggregation rewrite); SigNoz / OpenObserve / HyperDX / ClickStack = the OSS-ClickHouse-stack alternative (query-time aggregation on columnar storage, not push-time); Sawmills / Cribl / Edge Delta / Bindplane / ControlTheory = the telemetry-pipeline shapers that drop or aggregate metrics BEFORE the TSDB. For the OTel-native specifically: the spanmetrics connector + statsdreceiver + OTel metrics data-model spatial/temporal re-aggregation are the in-process incumbents - any team building 'shape metrics inside the collector before they hit storage' is using these primitives. M&A signal is unambiguous: Chronosphere = $3.35 B (largest pure-play observability M&A in the period); Splunk = $28 B (Cisco, 2024); New Relic = $6.5 B PE take-private (2023); Sumo Logic = $1.7 B PE; Honeycomb $50 M Series D 2023; Grafana Labs last private round $240 M Series D 2022 at $6 B (no public 2025-2026 round). The funding density and the specific 2025-2026 cadence (Mimir 3.0, Honeycomb Metrics GA, Chronosphere acquired, Last9 named Gartner Cool Vendor, Grafana Adaptive Telemetry, Sawmills emerging) say the segment is BOTH highly active and increasingly consolidating around two poles: 'OTel + PromQL + columnar storage' OSS and 'AI-era unified observability + security' proprietary.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed and a real wedge for beava. Apache-2.0 OSS dominant in the pure aggregator / pipeline shapers: VictoriaMetrics (community edition Apache-2.0; Enterprise license-key gated for downsampling, anomaly detection, multi-retention, LTS - a soft open-core), Cortex, Thanos, M3DB, SigNoz, OpenObserve, Sawmills (closed-source SaaS), Cribl (closed-source), Edge Delta (closed-source, but pipelines free-at-any-scale Apr 2026), Bindplane (Apache-2.0 OSS components). AGPLv3 in the Grafana stack: Mimir (AGPLv3 since 2021 relicense from Apache-2.0 of Cortex fork), Loki, Tempo, Grafana itself. Proprietary in the legacy big-three: Datadog, Splunk, Dynatrace, New Relic, plus Chronosphere (now Palo Alto Networks). Mixed in Honeycomb (proprietary product, Refinery tail-sampling tool open-source). Cardinality-shaping pipeline shapers Sawmills / Cribl / Edge Delta / Bindplane are mostly proprietary SaaS. Beava's Apache-2.0 + no-open-core is genuinely cleaner than Mimir (AGPLv3 has strict copyleft-on-network-service implications for embedders and vendors) and VictoriaMetrics Enterprise (open-core with paid downsampling). But the buyer in this segment is NOT primarily a vendor-OEM (where AGPL bites hardest) - it is platform-eng / SRE, who almost always run the observability stack as an internal service and for whom AGPL self-hosting is fine. So the license wedge is real but narrower than in the edge / rate-limit segment (V9). Where Apache-2.0 matters most: ISVs embedding observability into their product (the SaaS vendor selling a multi-tenant platform that wants per-tenant SLO counters in front of THEIR customers), and sovereign-edge / regulated EU buyers who want a clean OSS license posture across the entire stack.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium-to-High. Unlike the edge / rate-limit segment (V9) where every CDN bundles the primitive, observability bundling is concentrated in the hyperscaler-managed-Prometheus offerings (AWS Managed Service for Prometheus + Amazon CloudWatch, Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus + Cloud Monitoring, Azure Monitor + managed Prometheus) and in the big-three SaaS observability vendors (Datadog Metrics Without Limits, Splunk Observability Cloud, Dynatrace Davis, New Relic) PLUS Palo Alto Networks-Chronosphere as the new 'observability + security' bundle. Grafana Cloud Adaptive Telemetry is a SaaS-only bundled feature delivering 35% average metrics-cost reduction across 1,500+ orgs - this is exactly the buyer-default for any team already on Grafana Cloud. For the typical SRE / platform-eng buyer, the path of least resistance is: (1) already on Datadog, switch on Metrics Without Limits and accept the two-tier bill; (2) already on Grafana Cloud, enable Adaptive Metrics (free with the plan); (3) already on AWS, lean on Managed Prometheus + CloudWatch; (4) already on Palo Alto Networks (security), expand to Chronosphere via the unified bundle (post Jan 2026); (5) self-host VictoriaMetrics or Mimir and configure stream aggregation rules in YAML. Beava is structurally NOT on any of these paths today - it does not speak PromQL, does not export Prometheus remote-write, does not ship an OTel exporter, does not have a Grafana data-source plugin. The bundling threat compresses the winnable segment to: (a) ISV / SaaS-platform teams that need per-tenant counters in front of THEIR customers (where the SRE buyer becomes the platform-eng buyer and the observability tier is co-located with the application tier - this is closer to beava's natural fit); (b) self-hosted Kubernetes shops in regulated industries (finance, gov, EU-sovereign) that want a single-binary OSS stack and explicitly avoid managed observability SaaS; (c) inline admission-control / rate-limit gate buyers where the observability counter IS the gate counter (the edge / API-gateway overlap from V9 and V3). Threat is HIGHER than for fraud / ad-tech but LOWER than for edge rate-limit, because the buyer cares less about the binary primitive (counter) and more about the full chain (ingest + storage + PromQL + Grafana + alerting) - none of which beava ships.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: The mandatory front door for this segment is the OpenTelemetry Collector (OTLP/gRPC or OTLP/HTTP). Every named incumbent ships an OTel-collector exporter OR positions itself as OTel-native (SigNoz, OpenObserve, Dash0, Honeycomb, Chronosphere, Last9, Grafana, VictoriaMetrics). The supporting standards: Prometheus remote-write (the de facto interop format - any backend that does not accept it is excluded from the buyer's evaluation list), Prometheus scrape, statsd UDP (legacy but still common via OTel statsdreceiver), and CloudEvents (emerging for billing-meter-grade ingest). The shaping layer between source and storage typically runs in the collector itself (spanmetrics connector, statsdreceiver, attributesprocessor, filterprocessor, metricstransformprocessor, OTel temporal/spatial re-aggregation primitives) or in a dedicated pipeline product (Cribl, Sawmills, Edge Delta, Bindplane). Consumers downstream: PromQL-compatible alerting (Alertmanager, Grafana alerting), SLO platforms (Sloth, Pyrra, Nobl9), dashboards (Grafana - canonical, Datadog dashboards, Honeycomb boards), and AIOps / incident-response (Rootly, PagerDuty Event Intelligence, Datadog Watchdog). CRITICAL ASYMMETRY for beava: beava has NO OTel-collector exporter, NO Prometheus remote-write receiver, NO PromQL-subset query surface, NO Grafana data-source plugin, NO Alertmanager integration, and NO published OpenMetrics or OTLP scrape endpoint - in this segment those four-to-five missing pieces are roughly the entire integration surface the buyer expects. The Python SDK is the wrong language entirely for this audience (SREs use YAML config, PromQL, and Grafana JSON - not Python). The HTTP/JSON :8080 push-on-event model is conceptually fine but does not map to any standard collector exporter, so every adoption requires writing a custom OTel collector exporter shim - high friction. The framed-TCP+msgpack :8081 advantage is real for the inline admission-control sub-segment (the rate-limit / quota / SLO-burn-rate-threshold gate at the API gateway) but is meaningless for the pure 'feed my Grafana dashboard' path. The segment's strongest adoption lever for beava would be: a beava-side Prometheus remote-write receiver that quietly turns beava into a transparent pre-aggregator in front of the SRE's existing Prometheus + Grafana stack, with no app-side change - this would be the closest analog to Cribl's appeal.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Almost universally an external rules engine on the alerting side - Alertmanager / Grafana alerting / Datadog monitors / Dynatrace / Splunk built-in rule engines read PromQL-style expressions over the aggregated counters and fire to PagerDuty / Slack / webhook. Some adaptive-thresholding deployments couple to an ML detector (Datadog Watchdog, Dynatrace Davis AI, Grafana Adaptive Telemetry recommendations, Sawmills AI cardinality recommendations, Honeycomb's BubbleUp / Anomaly Detection, Chronosphere AI features post-Palo-Alto-Networks, AWS DevOps Guru) - beava can feed the rolling-window features but the scorer itself lives in the observability platform, not in beava. Pure feature-server / pre-aggregator role; beava is decoupled from the scoring engine. The seam is natural and identical across named incumbents - the only segment-specific twist is that for inline admission-control or per-tenant noisy-neighbour suppression, the scoring is deterministic threshold ('rps > N OR burn_rate > 14.4x AND budget_remaining < 50% => suspend') executed at the gate, not in the observability tier - which is exactly the path where beava's sub-ms read latency matters most.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: There is a real but narrow wedge if and only if beava is repositioned correctly. The primitives are an EXACT 1:1 match for what this segment needs: count, rate, velocity, sum, mean, n_unique (HLL is the canonical sketch for unique-user-per-tenant-per-minute), quantile (t-digest / DDSketch / HDR-histogram is the canonical sketch for latency p95/p99 percentiles), recency, distance - this is literally the 'streaming aggregation' primitive catalogue from Grafana Mimir + VictoriaMetrics + Last9 Levitate + OTel collector connector, exposed as a Python feature spec rather than YAML rule configs. Concrete reasons a buyer might pick beava: (1) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get latency for inline admission-control / per-tenant rate-limit / SLO-burn-rate-threshold gates - this is the regime Prometheus / Mimir / VictoriaMetrics are STRUCTURALLY NOT designed for (their published query latencies are 100ms-10s on high-cardinality recording rules), and where beava actually beats every named TSDB. The 'inline gate at the API gateway' use case is the strongest beava wedge in this segment. (2) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Mimir-cluster / Redis-cluster - Mimir 3.0 itself now requires Kafka as an async buffer between ingest and query; VictoriaMetrics is simpler but still typically deployed as vmagent + vminsert + vmstorage + vmselect; beava collapses both ingest and serve into one binary. Strongest against multi-component Mimir / Cortex / M3 / Thanos deployments at small-to-mid scale. (3) Apache-2.0 no open-core - strictly more permissive than Mimir (AGPLv3 since 2021), VictoriaMetrics Enterprise (open-core with paid downsampling / anomaly detection / multi-retention), DragonflyDB (BSL), Redis (RSALv2/SSPLv1/AGPLv3 tri-license). Comparable to SigNoz / OpenObserve / Cortex / Thanos / M3DB / VictoriaMetrics-OSS. Real procurement wedge for ISVs embedding observability into a product. (4) Push-on-event model maps to OTel-collector forward-style pipelines without a broker hop (no Kafka), which beats Mimir 3.0's new Kafka-buffered architecture for small-fleet deployments. (5) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives mean buyers can express R.E.D + Golden Signals + multi-window SLO burn-rate (Google SRE workbook formulation) + per-tenant velocity + percentile features without writing PromQL recording rules or Lua-on-Redis - the same expressive ceiling as VictoriaMetrics stream aggregation but reachable via Python rather than YAML. (6) Cardinality-survive architecture: (tenant_id x route x method x status_class) is a per-entity row in beava, not a per-time-series in the TSDB index, so the per-entity memory cost is bounded by row count rather than blowing up the index - this is exactly the architectural shape Last9 Levitate and Chronosphere and Honeycomb-events all argue is correct for high-cardinality. (7) Velocity / recency / distance primitives are first-class - 'rate-of-change of error_rate over last 30s' or 'time since last 5xx for this tenant' are feature reads in beava, where Prometheus must compute them on every query (expensive) and Redis must hand-roll Lua. CAVEAT: every one of these wedges is conditional on beava NOT being sold as 'the streaming-aggregation observability backend' (where it loses on integration / query / dashboard surface) but as 'the sub-ms pre-aggregation feature-store that sits BETWEEN the OTel collector and either Mimir/VictoriaMetrics or the API-gateway inline gate'. The honest framing is: beava is the 'hot feature row in front of the TSDB', not a TSDB replacement.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking adoption in this segment today, in rough order of pain: (1) No OpenTelemetry Collector exporter / receiver - DISQUALIFYING. Every named incumbent ships one. Without an OTel-OTLP/HTTP-or-gRPC adapter, beava cannot sit in the SRE's existing collector pipeline. This is the single biggest gap; an OTel exporter is the entire front door for this segment. (2) No Prometheus remote-write receiver - DISQUALIFYING. Would let beava sit transparently behind existing Prometheus scrape configs and aggregate at the (tenant, route) grain without any application change. Strongest single adoption lever for the SRE buyer and not in v0. (3) No PromQL / SQL query surface - the SRE buyer expects ad-hoc 'show me top 10 tenants by p95 latency in the last 10 minutes' queries; beava only serves the features it has been told to compute. This is a fundamental product gap for the 'replace my TSDB' framing and forces beava into the 'hot pre-aggregation tier in front of the TSDB' role - which can be the chosen positioning, but the buyer-education cost is high. (4) No Grafana data-source plugin - SREs visualise everything in Grafana; without a Beava data-source plugin OR a PromQL-subset proxy, beava features cannot show up on the dashboard. (5) No TLS, no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 in v0 - DISQUALIFYING for any production deployment handling request-level metadata across trust boundaries. Required before any vendor / partner / cross-team eval. (6) No in-process sharding - a single very large platform (>684 k EPS or tens of GB hot state per region) must hand-shard externally, whereas Mimir, VictoriaMetrics Cluster, Chronosphere, Datadog all shard internally. Mimir 3.0 (Nov 2025) just published 1 B active series per cluster - beava is structurally not in that league at v0. (7) No first-class multi-tenancy primitives (per-tenant namespaces, per-tenant write quotas, per-tenant rate-limit on beava's own ingress) - Mimir, Chronosphere and Datadog have entire control-plane sub-products for this; required for any vendor embedding beava across many customer workspaces. (8) No documented HLL / DDSketch / t-digest / HDR-histogram as first-class first-class aggregations prominently in the docs (the ~60-primitive catalogue may include them, but the latency-percentile story must be airtight for SRE buyers - averaging pre-computed percentiles is a textbook anti-pattern that immediately disqualifies a vendor). (9) No triggers / 'fire when feature crosses threshold' - SLO burn-rate alerting wants this natively ('fire when burn_rate_5m > 14.4x for 2m AND burn_rate_1h > 6x for 5m' is the Google SRE multi-window formulation). Today the alert evaluator has to poll, which is wasteful at 100k+ (tenant, route) keys. (10) No long-term archive sink (Mimir remote-write, S3/Parquet, ClickHouse) - the cold tier for 28-30 day SLO compliance reporting still lives elsewhere, so beava must dual-write or hand off, and there is no documented adapter. (11) No multi-window burn-rate / EWMA / Welford's online variance / streaming z-score as named first-class primitives - SRE buyers want 'multi-window burn rate' as a one-line feature spec, not a hand-built composition of count + window-arithmetic. (12) Refuse-on-network-FS / WAL-on-local-NVMe + single-binary single-region discipline is the right architectural posture but is operationally NEW to the SRE buyer who is used to multi-AZ-replicated Mimir / Cortex / VictoriaMetrics deployments; the runbook story (cold-start replay time SLO, snapshot cadence, eviction policy under cardinality pressure) needs to be airtight before SRE will trust beava as part of the alerting path. (13) No public SRE / observability case study, no beava OTel demo in python/beava/demos/, no observability-shaped reference architecture in docs/. The buyer needs to see 'request_completed event -> per-(tenant, route, method) rolling RPS + error_rate + p95 latency + SLO burn rate -> Grafana panel' as a runnable example. (14) Python SDK is wrong-language for the SRE audience - SREs configure observability in YAML / HCL / Helm, not Python. The wire is language-agnostic but the SDK gap is real. (15) No native multi-window burn-rate alerting language (Sloth / Pyrra / Nobl9-style) - if beava wanted to be SRE-native, multi-window-multi-burn-rate would be a built-in helper, not a hand-composed feature spec. (16) Wrong-buyer trap risk: the SRE buyer expects Prometheus-style PromQL + OTel ingestion + Grafana integration; beava ships none of these. The honest positioning is 'beava is for platform-eng teams who need per-tenant counters and don't want a full o11y platform' - but THAT buyer overlaps with V9 (edge / API-gateway rate-limit) much more than with the SRE-observability buyer.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Beava-side: NO public beava users in this segment identified. [uncertain] NO dedicated observability / per-tenant-RED / SLO-burn-rate demo in python/beava/demos/ at the time of review (existing demos are adtech / ecommerce / fraud per V9 review - none of these is the SRE shape). [uncertain] NO beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion threads on observability located. [uncertain] NO published OTel-collector exporter, NO Prometheus remote-write receiver, NO Grafana data-source plugin, NO PromQL-subset proxy, NO Alertmanager integration - the entire integration surface this segment expects. The use-case research (14_observability) correctly identifies the buyer (platform-eng / SRE - explicitly NOT the application developer reading dashboards, and explicitly NOT the risk / fraud team) and notes the same OTel-and-PromQL integration gap. External market validation that the SHAPE is right (but not that beava has traction): Grafana Mimir 3.0 launch at KubeCon NA Nov 2025 with MQE streaming + Kafka buffer + 1 B active series scale validates the architectural shape; Grafana Adaptive Telemetry at ObservabilityCON 2025 with 35% metrics-cost reduction across 1,500+ orgs validates the cardinality-shaping market urgency; Chronosphere $3.35 B acquisition by Palo Alto Networks (announced Nov 19 2025, completed Jan 29 2026) at $160 M+ ARR and triple-digit YoY growth definitively validates the cardinality-control segment as venture-grade and now strategic; Honeycomb Metrics GA Mar 11 2026 with hybrid time-series + events-based model validates the high-cardinality-first thesis; VictoriaMetrics' documented 4-second-to-fraction-of-a-second query speedups via stream aggregation, with real configs aggregating 114,765 series down to 785, validates the technical thesis; Last9 Levitate's 20 M+ cardinality-per-metric capability, Sequoia-India / Peak XV backing, Gartner Cool Vendor 'AI for SRE Observability' 2025 award, and public customer roster (Replit, Disney+ Hotstar, Clevertap, Circle, Probo, Quickwork) prove there is a venture-fundable challenger profile in this segment; Sawmills $10 M seed (Feb 2025) and Edge Delta's free-at-any-scale telemetry pipeline (Apr 2026) further validate that 'cut cardinality before storage' is a 2025-2026 race; the GitHub Mimir issues #12602 (ingester hitting series limits when scaling up), #12135 ('per-user series limit of 150,000 exceeded'), #1750 (reduce cardinality of metrics exposed by Mimir itself), #4108 (use estimated query cardinality in query sharding), and discussions #4590 / #3130 all describe per-tenant cardinality-explosion pain in production Mimir. The market validation is overwhelming and the technical thesis is exactly right; the beava-specific traction in this segment is zero, and the buyer-mismatch risk (SRE expects PromQL + OTel + Grafana, none of which beava ships) is real and explicitly flagged.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Watch (downgraded from Compete). The primitive catalogue match is uncanny - count / sum / mean / quantile / n_unique / velocity / recency map 1:1 to what every named incumbent (Mimir, VictoriaMetrics, Chronosphere, Last9 Levitate, Honeycomb-events, OTel-collector-spanmetrics) productises - AND the 2025-2026 market is unambiguously hot ($3.35 B Chronosphere acquisition, Mimir 3.0 launch, Honeycomb Metrics GA, Grafana Adaptive Telemetry, Last9 Gartner Cool Vendor). But the buyer-mismatch is structural: the SRE / platform-eng buyer expects PromQL + OTel ingestion + Grafana data-source + Alertmanager integration + multi-window burn-rate alerting language + multi-tenant control plane - beava ships LITERALLY NONE of these in v0. Building all of them is 6-12 months of work AND duplicates what the AGPLv3 Grafana stack, the Apache-2.0 VictoriaMetrics stack, and the Apache-2.0 SigNoz/OpenObserve ClickHouse stacks already ship today. The honest positioning is NOT 'beava is the SRE observability backend' but 'beava is the sub-ms feature-store that sits between the OTel collector and the API-gateway inline gate for per-tenant rate-limit / quota / SLO-burn-rate enforcement' - which is a much narrower wedge that overlaps with V9 (edge / API-gateway rate-limit) more than with the SRE-observability buyer. Recommend Watch, not Compete, because: (a) the buyer is wrong - SRE-observability is a different sales motion (YAML / Helm / PromQL / Grafana) than fraud / ad-tech / edge-rate-limit (Python / SDK / sub-ms TCP), (b) the integration debt to be credible is 6-12 mo and the resulting product would be a worse Mimir, (c) the segment is consolidating around two poles (OTel + PromQL OSS, and AI-era proprietary), neither of which beava plays in, (d) the wedge that IS real (sub-ms inline admission-control with per-tenant counters) is better captured under V9 (edge / API-gateway) where the buyer is platform-eng / API-gateway-vendor rather than SRE. Only upgrade to Compete IF beava explicitly repositions as 'the streaming pre-aggregation feature-store FOR API gateways doing inline per-tenant SLO-burn-rate enforcement, NOT a Mimir replacement' AND ships at minimum: OTel-collector exporter + Prometheus remote-write receiver + first-class multi-window-burn-rate primitive + DDSketch/HDR-histogram percentile docs + at least one runnable observability demo in python/beava/demos/. Avoid the 'wrong-buyer trap' is the dominant risk signal in this segment - the use-case research correctly identified it and the verdict honours it.
